accuracy.evidence: Matches EEF Metacognition and Self-Regulated Learning guidance (activate prior knowledge, make links explicit), elaborative encoding research (Craik & Lockhart; Dunlosky et al. 2013 elaborative interrogation and self-explanation) and schema theory (Bartlett, Rumelhart). Science links checked: bat wing has elongated finger bones (homologous with the hand), heart is a muscular pump with valves, compass needle is a magnet, sound spreads as vibrations, ships float despite their mass, plants make food by photosynthesis, not from soil.

misconceptions.evidence: Names and tests surface-feature links (colour, shape), feeling links, treating an analogy as an exact match, and building on misconceptions (heavy things sink, plants eat soil, multiplying always makes bigger) in the Helps or misleads step and mastery m3.

lab_distinct.evidence: New flaglink lab: matching new ideas to known ones, a same/not-same sort for an analogy's limits, a radial web builder and best-link rounds. Shingle check passed against all existing labs; different from the sorter visual and earlier L2L labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step practises one part of the strategy: link, test the limits, build several links, choose structural over surface links, check old ideas. Feedback says why a link works or misleads.

predictions.evidence: Predictions before steps 1, 2 and 4 ask which link fits, whether a heart is fully like a pump, and which link explains best; reveals compare the guess with the answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Challenge mixes all three link types with specific messages for each wrong choice; Show me finishes in under 2.3 s on every step.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and concrete examples for ages 7-8; adult text passes FK 10 and names the key terms (elaborative encoding, schema, analogy, prior knowledge, metacognition).

no_filler.evidence: Every card carries an example; no generic study-skills padding; family tip is a two-question routine.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360px Android and iPhone 13: cards and boxes are large, buttons stack, nothing overlaps or clips; tap and drag both work.

accessibility.evidence: axe clean in dark and light themes; canvas has an aria-label and live c.say text; all choices also work as buttons with no drag needed.

sources: Education Endowment Foundation (2018/2021) Metacognition and Self-Regulated Learning guidance report
Dunlosky et al. (2013) Improving students' learning with effective learning techniques, Psychological Science in the Public Interest
Rumelhart (1980) Schemata: the building blocks of cognition; Gentner (1983) Structure-mapping theory of analogy
